How Exhale Began

The journey to Exhale all started from a deep place of fellowship with God.

God gave a clear word to the convener: “I want you to host a healing meeting.” As clarity came, it became obvious that God was pointing more towards healing the parts that are not obvious to all. Particularly, Isaiah 61 was given, as it speaks to “binding up the brokenhearted.”

And so, through the instrument of worship, word, therapy, and meditation, we've seen many lives transformed. We've seen traumas healed, insight come to people in unusual ways, and the healing that goes deeper than any surgeon's knife happen repeatedly in these meetings. The transformation is always total: spirit, soul, and body — and it influences every aspect of our lives, including our relationships, businesses, families, and most importantly, our work with God.

We're excited for yet another breathtaking experience this season. We see this year's meeting impacting individuals, families, and generations.

From dysfunction to wholeness.
Oluwatobi Adesanya · Convener, Exhale

2026 Dysfunction to Wholeness
A Personal Invitation

For a long time, society has normalised dysfunction — patterns, belief systems, and mindsets that have quietly defined our marriages, our relationships, our purpose, and what we eventually became.

There's a man in Scripture I keep coming back to — the man at the pool of Bethesda. He was there for thirty‑eight years, an invalid, and he always had a reason ready: no one to help him in, no one to push him into the water. All kinds of excuses, back and forth, that kept him exactly where he was.

That's what dysfunction does — to individuals, to families, even to nations. We keep ourselves there. And dysfunction, by definition, simply means operating in a distorted version of the design God actually has for you.

Then Jesus walked up to that man and asked him a question that had nothing to do with the excuses: “Do you want to be made whole?”

That same question is what Exhale 2026 is built around. It's why we believe this isn't just a conference — it's a key tool for personal and family transformation, the kind that can eventually turn into something bigger than any one of us. Healing from relational trauma, family trauma, and all the mental health challenges life has handed us — some from upbringing, some from deprivation, some from things done to us as children.

God has a plan for you, though. He wants you made whole. So before this is an event, let me ask you the same question, one person to another.

Do you want to be made whole?
Oluwatobi Adesanya · Convener, Exhale

What we mean by “dysfunction”

Dysfunction, by definition, simply means operating in a distorted version of the design God actually has for you as a person. It's not a label for anyone in this room — it's something all of us deal with in one way or another. Society has normalised it for so long that most days, it just looks normal.

In a Person

Self‑worth

Self‑sabotage, the quiet belief that vulnerability isn't safe, the gap between who you present and who you actually are.

In a Relationship

What Love Runs On

Love built from old wounds instead of present clarity. Boundaries never learned. Trust rationed out instead of given.

In a Family

What Gets Inherited

A temper, a silence, a way of surviving that outlived its usefulness — passed down without ever being questioned.

Four Questions We Came Here To Ask

What patterns are shaping my life?

Where did they come from?

What have I normalised that needs to change?

What would wholeness actually look like for me?

The Shape of This Year's Journey
Awareness→ Understanding→ Healing→ Integration→ Wholeness→ Strength→ Impact
Who This Is For

It's for you, actually

Anyone tired of carrying the same weight into every new season.

Anyone who keeps repeating a pattern and doesn't know why.

Someone healing from heartbreak, or still rebuilding after something worse.

Someone whose family taught them dysfunction before it taught them anything else.

Someone who has everything working on paper, but still knows something inside needs attention.

And anyone already healing — who wants to become strong enough to help someone else.

The Experience

Not a stage to watch. A room to enter.

We built Exhale to be participatory — a programme that gives you room to listen, think, feel, reflect, pray, write, connect, and respond.

Exhale 2026 · Four Voices

Meet the Speakers

Different perspectives on one conversation — ministry, therapy, emotional health, and lived experience — so the sessions complement each other rather than repeat the same message.

Oluwatobi Adesanya
Convener · Journal Therapist

Curator of Journaling for Answers and visionary behind Exhale. Certified in journal therapy, walking people from trauma back to their own story.

Read moreShow less

He is certified in Journal Therapy by the Center of Excellence, UK, and trained in emotional therapy and counselling by Audacity2Lead Academy. For years, he has walked with people through trauma, heartbreak, and identity loss — helping them rewrite their internal narratives and recover their emotional wholeness.

Through platforms like Mental First Aid, he equips people with practical tools to process pain and find stability when their soul is under pressure. He is also CEO of Heart2World Publishing, helping authors birth transformational books, and leads coaching programmes and fellowships that merge spiritual maturity, emotional intelligence, and personal growth.

Doreen Omosele
TMA · Founder, Blossom Girls Outreach

Author of Warrior Woman. Has walked over 1,500 women out of the sex trade and into restoration through the Blossom Rehab centre.

Read moreShow less

In 2023 she established The Blossom Rehab, a centre offering healing, transformation, restoration, and financial empowerment to women who have exited prostitution. Her book Purple has brought hope to girls in the sex trade in five languages — English, Pidgin, Yoruba, Hausa, and Igbo.

She is President of When Ladies Gather and Convener of the annual Warrior Woman Conference. In 2024 she released her debut film, February 14th, and was nominated for The Future Awards Africa Community Action award; in 2025 she received the Governor Sanwo-Olu Social Impact Award. She also runs Narra Africa Media, and is happily married with three daughters.

Adebanjo Moyosore
Trauma Recovery Specialist

Founder, Relationship & Reality Consult. His own story of childhood abandonment shapes a mission — inspired by Isaiah 61 — to lead families from dysfunction to wholeness.

Read moreShow less

He initially trained as a violinist before God redirected him into healing and restoration work. Having experienced maternal and paternal abandonment in childhood, he has spent more than half a decade helping others recover from childhood trauma, attachment wounds, codependency, and unhealthy relationship patterns.

He is Founder of the HEARTRUB Conference and the Relationship & Reality Tribe, and serves as Assistant Music Director at Trinity House Church, Victoria Island. He studied at the University of Ibadan and the MUSON School of Music, holding distinctions from the Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music, London. He has authored several books, including 50 Red Flags You Must Take Before Getting Married.

Abimbola Durojaye
Family Counsellor · Director, Millhouse Schools

Certified Family Counsellor and Marriage Therapist, and Director of Millhouse Schools, Lagos — where she and her husband also serve as pastors at Spirit of Life Christian Center.

Read moreShow less

A Harvard‑trained educator and school leader, her expertise spans entrepreneurship, operational management, learning facilitation, and personal and spiritual development.

She is the author of two transformational books: Behind the Mask, which helps teenagers and young adults navigate self‑identity and personal awareness, and The Praying Parent: A 40‑Day Guide, a practical resource that equips parents to pray intentionally and strategically for their children. She also hosts the annual Praying Parent Conference.

Abimbola is married to Fisayo Durojaye, a venture capital expert and fellow pastor at Spirit of Life Christian Center. They live in Lagos with their children.

Minister Tobi Michael
Worship

A Nigerian gospel minister and self-described “Jesus addict,” known for leading deep worship through songs like Koinonia, Occupy, and You Are God — and for raising true worshippers wherever he leads.

That's the room waiting for you. Come meet them in person.
